chunks: From him, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Husayn, from Fudaylah, from Aban ibn 'Uthman, from al-Fadl ibn 'Abd al-Malik, who said:

I asked Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the travelers who differ [in their travel status], so he said, 'When they travel extensively, they should shorten [the prayer].' The meaning intended by these two narrations is that when the stay of these travelers in the city is more than ten days, shortening [the prayer] is obligatory upon them, just as it is obligatory upon the residents; and when their stay is less than that, full [prayer] is obligatory upon them, according to what we have previously mentioned. The meaning that indicates this is what was narrated:

key_terms.التَّقْصِيرُ: Shortening the four-rak'ah prayer to two rak'ahs
key_terms.الْمُكَارِينَ: Travelers who are uncertain about their travel status or duration
key_terms.عَشَرَةِ أَيَّامٍ: Ten days, the threshold for determining travel status

ai.seo_question: What is the prayer ruling for travelers who are unsure if their stay is short or long?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq clarifies the ruling for 'mukarin' (travelers with uncertain duration), establishing that a stay exceeding ten days mandates shortening prayers (qasr) as if they were residents, while shorter stays require full prayers (tamam). This ruling is foundational in Shia fiqh for determining the status of travelers who do not have a fixed destination or return date, linking the physical duration of stay directly to the obligation of prayer length.
